What changed, and why

Show the app before the details

Was

Product pages opened with text and missing screenshot slots.

Now

Each page opens with a real screenshot and gives access to the original image.

Keep release status clear

Was

Unreleased app listings had no useful feature overview.

Now

Radio Clip and Media Lab explain the development workflow and use explicitly labeled sample-data previews without download buttons.

Keep downloads tied to versions

Was

Offload could reuse an old requirement or download fallback when live metadata changed.

Now

Known requirements belong to the matching version; missing release assets do not produce a download action.

Verification

  • 39 focused tests passed on Node 22.23.3.
  • Production-shaped application build passed; TypeScript passed after build-generated files settled.
  • Repository lint: 0 errors, 43 pre-existing warnings. Documentation maps and git diff checks passed.
  • All five pages checked at 1280 × 720 and 390 × 844 without page overflow. Fetch workflow and original-image links work from the keyboard.
  • Light and dark appearance controls persist across reload. Phone screenshots stack vertically; the focused image fits fully within the viewport.

Things to know

  • The three new pages have after-only evidence; there was no previous product page to compare.
  • The preview uses static public content with no authenticated team or archive data. It does not prove native ingest, transcription accuracy or physical-device behavior.
  • Production publication and CI are pending at the time this review was prepared.

New product pages — after-only evidence

These three routes had no previous product page. Screenshots show the same local static-content renderer used in the comparisons.
